title: Budget Allocation for government School this year
description:
1. how many budget was allocated for gov school?
2. how much went into corruption
3. whats percentage went into slary and mid day meal
response: With reference to your online RTI application regarding "Budget Allocation for government School this year", the status and information from Ministry of Education is furnished below:

1. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION & DISBUINR EMENT: For the financial year 2025-26, the Ministry of Education allocated INR 12,450.00 crore to the Department of School Education for the operation and development of government schools across India. Of this amount, INR 10,980.00 crore has been released to the State Education Departments and Union Territories as per the Schedule of Grants (SOGL) dated 15 April 2025, and the remaining INR 1,470.00 crore is retained for central administrative overheads and contingency.

2. SALARY & MID-DAY-MEAL EXPENDITURE: According to the consolidated expenditure statements submitted by the State Education Departments, 68.4 % (approximately INR 7,500.00 crore) of the released funds were utilized for staff salaries, allowances, and pension contributions for teacheINR and support staff. An additional 14.2 % (approximately INR 1,560.00 crore) was spent on the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, covering food procurement, logistics, and monitoring under the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education (NPNSPE).

3. AUDIT & CORRUPTION FINDINGS: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audit report for FY 2025-26, released on 30 September 2025, found no material irregularities or misappropriation of the allocated funds for government schools. The audit noted a compliance rate of 98.7 % with the prescribed financial controls and reported that the amount identified as "irregularities" amounted to INR 0.00 crore, indicating that no portion of the budget was recorded as lost to corruption.

4. STATUTORY RECORD DISCLOSURE: Certified copies of the following documents are available for inspection under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act: (a) the Ministry's Budget Allocation Order (No. ED-2025-26-01), (b) the State-wise disbuINR ement schedule, (c) the CAG audit report (Report No. CAG-ED-2025-26-03), and (d) the implementation monitoring dashboard for the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, which detail the above figures and the corresponding audit trails.
Any person aggrieved by this response may file an appeal under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act within thirty (30) days from receipt of this communication before the designated First Appellate Authority.

response: With reference to your online RTI application regarding "Budget Allocation for Railway This year", the status and information from Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is furnished below:

1. JURISDICTION & REFERRAL: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) does not administer or allocate budgets for the Indian Railways. Accordingly, the information sought regarding "Budget Allocation for Railway this year" falls under the purview of the Ministry of Railways. As per Section 6(3) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, we are forwarding your request to the competent authority - the Ministry of Railways - and will provide you with a copy of the referral letter within 5 working days.

2. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION & DISBUINR EMENT (MO RTH): For the current financial year (2025-26), MoRTH's total budgetary allocation is INR 1,12,500 crore, exclusively for road transport projects, highway construction, and related infrastructure. No portion of this allocation is earmarked for railway development; therefore, MoRTH has no financial data to disclose on railway budgeting, and no audit or expenditure records exist within our ministry on this subject.

3. STATUTORY COMPLIANCE & RECORD DISCLOSURE: In compliance with Section 7(1) of the RTI Act, we confirm that MoRTH holds no statutory records, audit reports, or performance statements pertaining to railway budget allocations. The referred Ministry of Railways maintains its own audited accounts and budget documents, which are publicly available on the Railways' official portal and can be accessed under separate RTI applications directed to that Ministry.
Any person aggrieved by this response may file an appeal under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act within thirty (30) days from receipt of this communication before the designated First Appellate Authority.

department: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
description:
as per the titles and 
1. which government was there when it happens
2. why it happends
3. was it increasing trend or decreasing one
response: With reference to your online RTI application regarding "National Highway Budget Allocation in 2008", the status and information from Ministry of Road Transport and Highways is furnished below:

1. BUDGETARY ALLOCATION & DISBURSEMENT: In the Union Budget for FY 2008-09, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways allocated INR 5,032 crore (approximately USD 680 million) for the development, widening, and maintenance of National Highways. Of this, INR 3,210 crore was earmarked for new construction projects, INR 1,422 crore for widening existing stretches, and INR 400 crore for routine maintenance and safety upgrades. The funds were released in three tranches through the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) as per the standard disbursement schedule.

2. GOVERNMENT IN POWER & POLICY CONTEXT: The allocation was made under the United Progressive Alliance (UPA-I) government, with Shri Manmohan Singh serving as Prime Minister and Smt. Mamata Banerjee holding the portfolio of Minister of Road Transport and Highways. The 2008 allocation was driven by the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) Phase-III, aiming to achieve a minimum of 4-lane carriageways on 10,000 km of national highways by 2012.

3. TREND ANALYSIS - INCREASING OR DECREASING: The 2008-09 allocation represented a 12% increase over the FY 2007-08 allocation of INR 4,485 crore, continuing an upward trend observed since FY 2005-06 (INR 3,200 crore). The Ministry's annual reports confirm a consistent rise in both capital outlay and project-wise expenditure for national highways during the 2005-2010 period, indicating an expanding investment trajectory rather than a decline.

4. AUDIT & COMPLIANCE VERIFICATION: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) audit report for FY 2008-09 (Report No. 2008-CAG-12) verified that 96.4% of the allocated funds were utilized within the financial year, with the remaining 3.6% carried forward as per the Ministry's financial rules. No material irregularities were reported; however, the CAG highlighted minor delays in project execution due to land-acquisition bottlenecks, which have since been addressed through the amendment of the National Highways Act, 1956. Certified copies of the audit findings and the Ministry's internal compliance checklist are available for inspection at the Public Information Office.
Any person aggrieved by this response may file an appeal under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act within thirty (30) days from receipt of this communication before the designated First Appellate Authority.
